passage:
The computer lab closed at nine, Tarun's data pack had almost run out, and the problem set was due at midnight. Tarun worked through question after question by hand, erasing and trying again, hunched over one desk in a noisy corridor.

Across the room, Anand finished the whole set in ten minutes with an AI tool, closed the laptop and left for tea. Next week the marks came back: Anand scored higher. Tarun felt foolish, as if hours of effort had bought nothing.

A month later, at a mock interview, the panel asked Anand to explain one solution on the whiteboard. Anand's marker stayed still.

Tarun, on the other hand, had used the AI as a tutor that night, asking it to explain the one step that didn't click, and could walk through every line.

qa.q: What time did the computer lab close?
qa.a: The computer lab closed at nine.

qa.q: How did Tarun feel when the marks came back, and why?
qa.a: Tarun felt foolish, as if hours of effort had bought nothing, because Anand scored higher after finishing in ten minutes.

qa.q: What did Tarun do with the AI that helped later?
qa.a: Tarun used it as a tutor to explain the one step that didn't click, so Tarun could walk through every line, while Anand copied without understanding.

qa.q: How might Anand feel at the mock interview?
qa.a: Anand probably felt exposed and stuck, with the marker staying still, because the shortcut left no understanding to explain.

grounding: Tarun envies Anand's quick, high-scoring AI work and feels foolish, but shortcuts show at the interview while using AI as a tutor builds real skill.

qa.q: How long did Mohit take to finish the stats assignment?
What was Sarita feeling after seeing Mohit's score?

qa.q: What would you advise someone in Sarita's place?

qa.q: How does Ganga see Sarita's 7 compared with Mohit's 9?

grounding: The chat shows a student envious of a classmate's fast AI work who decides to build real skill and use AI as a tutor instead of copying.

passage:
In the polytechnic in Sagar, marks were pinned on a board outside the staff room. Kunal had topped the electrical drawing assignment again. Gautam knew how: Kunal pasted every question into an AI tool on his phone during the bus ride and copied the diagrams at the canteen.

Gautam had spent Sunday at his uncle's workshop, rewiring a motor by hand, and scored eleven marks less. Walking home past the paddy fields, he felt hot and small. Why bother?

That night he opened the same AI tool. His finger hovered. Then he thought about next month's practical exam, where they would stand at a real panel with the instructor watching, no phones allowed.

He typed instead: "Explain why my circuit in question three was wrong. Don't give me the answer." The explanation took twenty minutes to understand. He drew it three times.

qa.a: Gautam spent Sunday at his uncle's workshop, rewiring a motor by hand.

qa.q: How was Gautam feeling walking home past the paddy fields?
qa.a: Gautam felt envious, hot and small, wondering why he bothered working hard when Kunal scored higher by copying.

qa.q: What small step helped Gautam use the tool wisely?
qa.a: Gautam asked the AI to explain his mistake without giving the answer, so he learned the circuit himself before the practical exam.

qa.q: How might Kunal feel at the practical exam with no phones allowed?
qa.a: Kunal may feel nervous and exposed if he has not really learned the diagrams he copied.

grounding: The story shows a young man envious of a classmate's AI shortcuts who chooses to build real skill and use AI as a tutor.
